scope: Explicit bounded kernel heap checks in Spectra CHECK MEMORY /KERNELHEAP.

implementation.ownership: Spectra owns selection, presentation and explicit export. Privileged allocation, exact cleanup and small shared case bodies stay at the kernel allocator owner.
implementation.cases: Reuse Rust alloc/realloc/dealloc, 24/400/6000-byte patterns, 4096 alignment, duplicate-free rejection, 2000-op/200-slot churn, 16x192-KB acceptance and 257-page resident commit/rollback/zero/physical-preflight cases. Boot wrappers use the same case bodies.
implementation.balance: One resident ledger retains exact own pointer/request/Layout and VM reservation identities. Own successful returns determine cleanup; global heap before/after values are observations. No global reset or new timing workload.
implementation.concurrency: Normal allocator users contend only on the existing allocator owner. CAS serializes diagnostics. The exact task unwind token spans allocation waits, cleanup and public output; no Runtime owner spans work. The tiny Rust dispatch proof briefly keeps the allocator owner and never waits. Other cases allow normal allocation waits; Close is polled cooperatively.
implementation.deliberate_errors: Both duplicate frees share the original allocator owner and validation/release function, before reuse or uncommit. Impossible physical commit requests exceed total frames, preserving impossibility despite foreign frees. Expected duplicate-free and VM rejections are separate from cleanup failures.
implementation.failed_cleanup: An unacknowledged own release retains its exact resident diagnostic identity and blocks further work. No blind retry against a potentially reused pointer and no false cleanup-success flag.
implementation.api: Contract 0.64.12 appends R4DEV v15 slot48 after the preserved 400-byte layout prefix, total408. New fixed ProgramKernelHeapCheck v1 is168bytes. Existing slots/types/constants are unchanged; explicit prefix audit precedes controlled baseline refresh. SDK0.64.24 exposes the optional typed call and existing availability errors.
implementation.presentation: Text and common NDJSON/EXPORT use the same structured result. Reject mixed unknown check options before work. Each request checks invalid header/capacity output preservation and a larger caller-buffer tail canary.
implementation.packaging: Include existing manifest-derived Version.zig in the Spectra package paths. The STANDARD method and frozen child remain unchanged.
implementation.rust_receipt: Retain the allocator owner across actual rustc void dealloc and exact free/coalesced/tail-removed metadata validation. The tiny three-dispatch Rust case also retains its original before/after counter oracle under that owner, so foreign activity cannot alter it. Normal allocator contention is bounded; this narrow case does not wait. Failed proof retains historical run-bound addresses without blind retries.
implementation.coalescing: Invalidate the old interior used header when a released block merges with its free predecessor, preserving fast normal validation and correct duplicate-free classification. Diagnostic Rust return receipts walk actual block boundaries; the aligned duplicate-free subcase covers prefix coalescing after retaining the original small alignment request.

initial_guest.finding: The allocation returned and owner-protected global usage balanced, but a stale interior header made the first diagnostic receipt fail. The retained failed run blocked the second request, which reported the same run_id instead of reusing the pointer. Bad-argument rejection passed. Correct boundary walking and interior-header invalidation require a rebuilt kernel and renewed heap checks.

This single-run difference remains visible without causal attribution; no benchmark-method change or extra run to improve scores. Frozen child unchanged.

performance_assessment: Allocator release factoring, shared kernel checks and an additive platform table change the normal artifact; exactly one final Suite-2 STANDARD SMP4 is required.
limits: The tiny Rust dispatch proof holds the ordinary allocator owner and cannot wait for growth; allocation failure remains an incomplete check with owned cleanup, not a global leak inference.
A rejected cleanup remains retained for allocator-owner investigation, never forcibly freed or hidden by resetting counters.
Scoped R4X terminal checks run after memory/tasks/services initialization on a nonempty heap; they are not BootReady conformance.
No global memory/backing/reclaim catalog, browser campaign, physical hardware or Windows-host claim.
One STANDARD is a descriptive single-run observation, not a causal performance estimate. Full exports/raw samples stay outside Git.
